title: Spec of a ring map induces that ring map on global sections
statement: Let $\psi:C\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\operatorname{Spec}\psi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ the induced morphism of schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\varepsilon_B:B\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B})$ and $\varepsilon_C:C\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}C,\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}C})$ be the canonical isomorphisms of rings, and $(\operatorname{Spec}\psi)^\sharp:\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}C,\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}C})\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B})$ the ring map induced by $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ on global sections. Then $(\operatorname{Spec}\psi)^\sharp\circ\varepsilon_C=\varepsilon_B\circ\psi$; that is, under the identifications of the rings of global sections with $C$ and $B$, the map induced by $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ on global sections is $\psi$.
